findings.title: Interactive controls have no accessible name
findings.description: 6 visible interactive element(s) expose no accessible name.
findings.inference: These are almost always icon-only controls — a hamburger menu, a close button, a search icon — where the icon is rendered as an SVG or a background image with no text alternative. Sighted users read the icon; assistive technology has nothing to read.

findings.impact: A screen reader announces these as "button" or "link" with no name. In a page with several, the user cannot distinguish between them at all.
findings.recommendation: Add `aria-label` describing the action ("Close dialog", "Open navigation menu", "Search"), or include visually-hidden text inside the control. For SVG icons, `<title>` inside the SVG plus `role="img"` also works.

findings.title: "View All Organizations" triggers a failing request (network error)
findings.description: Clicking "View All Organizations" issued a request to /api/dashboard/summary which failed (net::ERR_ABORTED).
findings.inference: The request the control depends on did not succeed, so the action it represents did not complete.
findings.technicalDetails:
Control: div > section:nth-of-type(1) > div > div:nth-of-type(7) > a
Request: GET https://ngo-ups3.onrender.com/api/dashboard/summary
Response: none
Outcome classification: NAVIGATED
DOM mutations observed: 52
findings.impact: The user journey that runs through this control is broken. If the UI does not surface the failure, users will believe the action succeeded — which is worse than an obvious error.
findings.recommendation: Confirm /api/dashboard/summary is the correct endpoint and that the request shape matches what the server expects. Add explicit error handling on the client.

findings.title: Cookies are missing security attributes
findings.description: 3 cookie(s) observed; 0 without Secure, 3 without HttpOnly, 3 without a restrictive SameSite.
findings.inference: `Secure` stops the cookie being sent over plain HTTP. `HttpOnly` stops JavaScript reading it, which is what limits the damage of an XSS flaw to actions rather than session theft. `SameSite=Lax` or `Strict` stops it being attached to cross-site requests, which is the main structural defence against CSRF. We can observe which attributes are set but not what each cookie is used for — a missing HttpOnly on an analytics cookie is unremarkable, on a session cookie it is serious.
findings.technicalDetails:
_tccl_visitor                secure=true  httpOnly=false sameSite=None
_tccl_visit                  secure=true  httpOnly=false sameSite=None
_scc_session                 secure=true  httpOnly=false sameSite=None
findings.impact: Where any of these cookies carries a session, the missing attributes translate directly into session theft via XSS, session leakage over HTTP, or CSRF.
findings.recommendation: Set `Secure; HttpOnly; SameSite=Lax` on every session and authentication cookie. Where a cookie must be readable by client-side script, confirm that is genuinely required — it usually is not.

findings.title: No XML sitemap found
findings.description: No sitemap was found at /sitemap.xml, /sitemap_index.xml, or referenced from robots.txt.
findings.inference: A sitemap gives search engines an explicit list of URLs to crawl along with change frequency hints. Without one, crawlers rely entirely on following links — so pages that are poorly linked internally, or newly published, are discovered slowly or not at all.
findings.technicalDetails: Probed /sitemap.xml and /sitemap_index.xml; neither returned a parseable sitemap.
findings.impact: Slower discovery and indexing of new or deeply-nested pages.
findings.recommendation: Generate an XML sitemap and reference it from robots.txt with a `Sitemap:` directive. Most frameworks and CMSs can produce one automatically.

findings.title: No Permissions-Policy header
findings.description: The `permissions-policy` response header is not set.
findings.inference: Permissions-Policy lets a site declare which powerful browser features (camera, microphone, geolocation, payment) may be used, including by embedded third-party frames. Without it, any embedded content can request those permissions in the site's name.
findings.technicalDetails:
Response headers observed on the document request:
  alt-svc
  cache-control
  cf-cache-status
  cf-ray
  content-encoding
  content-type
  date
  last-modified
  nel
  report-to
  server
  server-timing
  vary
findings.impact: This is a missing defence-in-depth control rather than an exploitable vulnerability on its own. It increases the damage another flaw could do.
findings.recommendation: Add a Permissions-Policy disabling features the site does not use, e.g. `Permissions-Policy: camera=(), microphone=(), geolocation=()`.
